monohydrate yields 3.4 calories per gram. As with amino acids, 
a 10% solution yields 100 g of carbohydrates per liter of solu-
tion. The use of carbohydrates (100 g daily for a 70-kg person) 
ensures that protein is not catabolized for energy during condi-
tions of normal metabolism.
Maximum rates of carbohydrate administration should not 
exceed 5 to 6 mg/kg/min in critically ill patients. When PN solu-
tions provide 15% to 20% of total calories as protein, 20% to 
30% of total calories as lipid, and the balance from carbohydrate 
(dextrose), infusion of dextrose should not exceed this amount. 
Excessive administration can lead to hyperglycemia, hepatic 
abnormalities, or increased ventilatory drive (see Chapter 34).
